test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 05 Dec 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

I had walked / for most of the day / to Kanpur and then / get on the train by Mumbai.

options.text: get on the train by Mumbai

solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **get on the train by Mumbai**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Replace "**get**" with "**got**" and "**by**" with "**to**" to correct the sentence.
 
• "**Had + v3**" is used in the past perfect tense to make it clear that one event happened before another in the past.
 
• In such sentences, the first action is written in the **past perfect** and second action in the **simple past** **tense**.
 
• So, "**got**" should be used here in the given sentence.
 
• The preposition **'to' **will be used instead of 'by' as it means** in the direction of**.
 
 
• Example: We went** to** Prague last year.
 
 
 
• We use "by + noun" to describe how someone travels or communicates, or how things are processed. (by car, by train etc.)
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 3** which contains an error in it.
 
• **The implied meaning of the sentence is:** I had travelled to Kanpur on foot for the majority of the day before boarding the train to Mumbai.

 

**Corrected sentence:** *I had walked for most of the day to Kanpur and then got on the train to Mumbai.*
